title: NFL Logo Quiz Part 2: Hard Mode
headline: NFL Logo Quiz Part 2: Name The Team From A Tiny Piece Of Its Logo
description: A hard NFL logo quiz: eight tiny pieces of NFL team logos, about 2% of each logo. Guess the team, tap to reveal the answer, keep score and share your result.
intro: Every piece below is a small square cut from a current NFL team logo, about one fiftieth of the whole mark. No full letters, no team names, no giveaways. Each piece still holds one real detail, a color pair, a curve or an edge that belongs to only one team.
Make your guess, then tap Show The Answer. Be honest and mark whether you got it, and your score adds up at the bottom.

items.piece: The gray ring around the logo, with its thin black edge.
items.fact: The Steelers' logo is based on the steel industry's Steelmark and was first worn in 1962. It sits only on the right side of the helmet.

items.piece: One of the white nail holes in the blue horseshoe.
items.fact: The horseshoe made the move with the Colts from Baltimore to Indianapolis in 1984 and is still the team's logo.

items.piece: The hilt of one of the crossed swords, beside the silver helmet on the black shield.
items.fact: Al Davis added the shield logo after taking over in 1963. It shows a helmeted pirate with an eye patch over two crossed swords.

items.piece: The left tip of the lightning bolt, gold inside powder blue.
items.fact: The Chargers updated their bolt in March 2020, before moving into SoFi Stadium, dropping the navy outline and leaning into powder blue.

items.piece: The horse's orange eye, inside the navy outline of its head.
items.fact: The Broncos unveiled this horse head on February 4, 1997. It replaced the old orange horse and moved the team to navy blue.

items.piece: A white corner inside the B, between a black and an orange stripe.
items.fact: The tiger-striped B became the Bengals' primary logo in 2004, replacing the leaping tiger the team had used since 1997.

items.piece: Gold, black and purple feathers at the top of the raven's head.
items.fact: The Ravens switched to this raven head in 1999 after an artist won a lawsuit over their original Flying B shield logo.

items.piece: The facemask bars, white with brown outlines, at the front of the helmet.
items.fact: The Browns are the only NFL team with no logo on the helmet, so the plain orange helmet is the logo. In 2015 it got a brighter orange and a brown facemask.
